title: WPSS/1583/2018 of Davki Devi Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1583 (S/S) of 2018
Davki Devi .....Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and Others ....Respondents
Mr. Deep Chandra Joshi, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, Deputy Advocate General for the State.

Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 The petitioner is a widow. The contention of the
petitioner is that her late husband was appointed in District
Jail, Barielly (U.P.) as Bandirakshak as back as on
01.04.1979. After completing 16 years of service, her
husband was given the benefit of the first promotional pay
scale. Thereafter, after completion of 19 years of service, he
had been given the benefit of one increment in the first
promotional pay scale. The petitioner's case is that, on
01.04.2004, her husband had completed 24 years of service
and her husband was entitled to be promoted as a Sub-Jailer
and he was also entitled to get the salary in the pay scale of
Rs.5000-150-8000/- (pre revised), which was otherwise
admissible on completion of 24 years of service.
2. As per the petitioner's counsel, the cadre structure
of the promotional scale in the department as adopted by the
respondents he was entitled to be paid the pay scales of
Rs.5,000-8,000/- w.e.f. 01.04.2004.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner contends
that the said benefit has not been extended to her late

2
husband, though her husband has died on 05.02.2014. The
learned counsel for the petitioner submits that she being the
widow of the deceased employee, she was entitled for the
benefit of second promotional pay scale of Rs.5000-150-
8000/- which is being paid to Sub-Jailer on completion of 24
years of service which her husband was deprived of and
consequential revision of pension. Hence she has preferred
the present writ petition.
4. In support of her contention, learned counsel for
the petitioner has placed on record the judgment as rendered
by this Court in Writ Petition No.199 (S/S) of 2009, Bhuvan
Chandra Pathak vs. State and others, as well as, the judgment
of the Coordinate Bench of this Court earlier rendered in
Writ Petition No.1709 (S/S) of 2014 on 11.09.2014. The
matter was heard in pre-lunch session and it was posted in the
post-lunch session to enable the learned Standing Counsel to
go through the records and to ensure as to whether the
controversy and relief sought for by the petitioner is covered
by the two judgments.
5. On the revival of the proceedings in the post-lunch session, the learned counsel for the respondents
submits that the relief sought and the controversy as sought
to be agitated and redressed by the petitioner from this Court
is squarely covered by the judgment passed by the
Coordinate Bench of this Court rendered on 19.07.2013 and
11.09.2014.

3
6. In view of the above terms and statement of
respondents' counsel Mr. N.S. Pundir that the controversy
stands covered by the aforesaid two judgments. The writ
petition too would stand disposed off in terms of the
judgment dated 19.07.2013 and 11.09.2014. Accordingly, a
writ of mandamus is issued commanding the respondents to
give the benefit of the second promotional pay scale of
Rs.5000-150-8000/- which was otherwise liable to be paid to
the late husband of the petitioner on satisfactory completion
of 24 years of service and to revise pensionery benefits
thereafter and pay revised pensionary benefit regularly and
its arrears within a period of six weeks from today.
7. Subject to the above observations, writ petition is
accordingly allowed. However, there would be no order as
to costs.
